choisir-couleur-cadran.title: Which dial colour should you choose?
choisir-couleur-cadran.description: Black, blue, green or light: choose a colour you will enjoy wearing, not just photographing.

sections.title: Think about Monday, not one special outfit
paragraphs: A colour can look irresistible in a photograph. The next question is whether you want to see it on your wrist with your everyday clothes. Look at your jacket, shoes and the jewellery you already wear. You do not need to match everything; aim for a combination that feels natural.

For your only watch, compare two different directions: a dark dial and a light one. If you already enjoy wearing a black watch, blue or green may add more variety than another nearly identical design.

sections.title: Black, blue or green: keep the design constant
paragraphs: The Tsuyosa family lets you compare colour without changing the whole watch. Tempus lists NJ0150-81E in black, NJ0150-81L in blue and NJ0150-81X in green. The three options below share a steel silhouette, while the dial changes the first impression.

Black can sit comfortably alongside very different outfits. Blue adds colour without necessarily becoming the centre of attention. Try green against the clothes you actually wear: a shade you love in a close-up can feel different on a wrist. These are style suggestions, not rules.

sections.title: Light, gold-tone and mother-of-pearl: name the right part
paragraphs: A gold-tone bracelet does not mean a gold dial. A watch can combine a silver dial, a gold-tone case and a leather strap. Cadrin’s dial-colour filter follows the dial described by Tempus, rather than the dominant colour in a photograph.

Colour families group several shades: navy and light blue both appear under Blue. Finish matters too. Sunray, matte and mother-of-pearl describe different surfaces. Open the exact photographs and specifications rather than deciding from a colour name alone.

sections.title: The last filter: reading the time at a glance
paragraphs: Look at the hands, markers and dial together. A dial you love should also let you find the time easily. A well-lit frontal photograph does not represent every lighting condition; look at other views when available.
Keep three references, compare colour, size and bracelet, then return to the one you want to wear tomorrow. A colour filter helps shorten the list. Your own preference makes the choice.

g-shock-montre-jeune.title: G-Shock or retro Casio: a watch with character
g-shock-montre-jeune.description: For a teenager, a student or anyone after a casual watch: three directions to compare before choosing.

sections.title: Start with style, not age
paragraphs: There is no single watch for every young person. Some like a bold sports shape, others a small retro digital, and others want hands. For a gift, notice what the recipient wears and ask which display they enjoy: digits, hands or both.

Think about the complete budget too. A watch someone feels happy wearing every day can be more useful than one chosen only to impress. Include delivery and check exchange terms before adjusting a bracelet.

sections.title: Three moods, three shapes
paragraphs: The GA-2100-1A1ER stands out through its octagonal case and all-black design. Hands sit alongside a small digital display. It suits someone looking for a recognisable G-Shock design without a smartwatch screen.

The GBD-200-2ER prioritises a digital display and activity-related functions. Before buying for connectivity, check the app’s services and phone compatibility. The F-91W-1YEG takes a different route with a retro resin silhouette: Casio dates the F-91W family’s launch to 1989.

sections.title: A sporty watch is not always a GPS watch
paragraphs: Bluetooth describes a phone connection, not a GPS receiver inside the watch. For the GBD-200, Casio describes using smartphone GPS to calibrate distance measurements from the accelerometer. That is different from recording a route with built-in GPS.

Likewise, the G-Shock name does not replace the model’s instructions for water, buttons and care. Choose the functions you will actually use. A longer specification sheet is not automatically more useful.

sections.title: Three checks before giving one
paragraphs: Compare size with a watch the recipient already wears. Look at the clasp and adjustment options. If colour is uncertain, let them choose: black and a vivid colour do not play the same role in an outfit.
A screen does not automatically make a watch a child-safety or location device. If that is the intended use, verify the exact service, phone or subscription requirements and limitations.

sections.title: Two black GA-2100s to compare
paragraphs: Prefer all black or lighter hour markers? Compare the exact 1A1ER and 1AER before choosing.

premiere-montre-haut-de-gamme.title: Your first higher-end watch: where should the money go?
premiere-montre-haut-de-gamme.description: A bracelet you love, a movement you enjoy or a particular finish: decide what spending more should add.

sections.title: The word luxury cannot choose for you
paragraphs: There is no universal price that turns a watch into a luxury watch. For a more substantial first purchase, replace the label with something tangible: a bracelet construction you enjoy, a captivating dial, a movement you want to look at or a shape you expect to keep wearing.
Write down what your current watch is missing. If nothing comes to mind, liking a new design is a perfectly valid reason. That pleasure does not need to be disguised as a technical necessity.

sections.title: Three references to clarify your priorities
paragraphs: The quartz PRX puts bracelet design at the centre while keeping quartz operation. The Khaki Field H70455533 goes in another direction: leather, a field-watch dial and an automatic movement. Use the Tsuyosa as a counterpoint: before spending more, notice what you already like in its steel silhouette.

These models do not represent the whole of fine watchmaking. They offer three concrete starting points at Tempus for deciding whether your interest lies in shape, movement or material. Card prices are dated observations, not availability promises.

sections.title: Look at the details you will touch every day
paragraphs: The clasp, crown and first bracelet links deserve as much attention as the dial. Try fastening, setting and slipping the watch under a cuff. Total weight alone does not describe its balance on your wrist.

Sapphire, an exhibition back and a long power reserve can appeal for different reasons. None proves superior overall finishing by itself. Compare exact references rather than transferring specifications from another size or movement within the same collection.

sections.title: Buy it to wear it
paragraphs: We do not present these watches as financial investments. Keeping the box and documents is useful but does not guarantee easy resale or a rise in value. Plan for appropriate maintenance and ask for a quote when work is needed.
Before paying, check the reference, applicable warranty, lead time and returns. If one of these watches already appeals strongly, you do not need to spend more to make the choice respectable.

squelette-coeur-ouvert-tourbillon.title: Skeleton, open-heart or tourbillon: which mechanism are you seeing?
squelette-coeur-ouvert-tourbillon.description: An opening in a dial can be fascinating. Understand what it reveals without paying for the wrong label.

sections.title: Open-heart: a window in the dial
paragraphs: An open-heart watch reveals part of the mechanism through an opening in the dial. The movement becomes part of the view without replacing the entire dial with visible gears. This can suit someone who enjoys watching a mechanism while still wanting a recognisable dial.
The Bambino Open Heart RA-AG0002S offered by Tempus illustrates this approach. Do not confuse it with the full-dial Bambino RA-AC0M04Y: one family can include different constructions and references.

sections.title: Skeleton: more of the mechanism in the design
paragraphs: A skeleton presentation opens up more of the view onto the movement. It also changes the background against which you read the hands. Look at contrast and markers, not just the effect in an enlarged photograph.
The two alternatives below compare open-heart and skeleton presentations. Neither is presented here as a tourbillon.

sections.title: Tourbillon: a different construction
paragraphs: A tourbillon places elements of the regulating mechanism, including the balance and escapement, in a moving cage. Breguet dates Abraham-Louis Breguet’s patent to 26 June 1801. The principle addressed rate variations linked to vertical positions in pocket watches.

Seeing a balance moving through a dial opening therefore does not identify a tourbillon. The term names a construction, not just a decorative opening. Nor does the label alone prove better accuracy than another watch in your own use.

sections.title: What can you choose at Tempus?
paragraphs: We identified no reference explicitly described as a tourbillon in the Tempus catalogue checked for this guide. We therefore do not relabel a skeleton watch to fill that category. If your main wish is to see the mechanism, open-heart and skeleton models remain genuine alternatives with their own visual appeal.
Before deciding, look at a face-on image at normal size, the strap material and case dimensions. Enjoying the mechanism should go alongside enjoying the fit and reading the time.

montre-connectee-gps-bluetooth.title: Connected watch, GPS or Bluetooth: choose the right function
montre-connectee-gps-bluetooth.description: Notifications, activity tracking and built-in GPS are not interchangeable. Two options at Tempus to match your actual needs.

sections.title: Start with the task
paragraphs: Reading notifications, counting steps and recording a route are three different needs. Before comparing screens, write down the one that matters most. If you mainly want the time without reaching for a phone, a conventional watch may already do the job.
For a connected watch, check phone compatibility, the required app and functions supported by your system. A listed feature does not mean every service works without a phone, connection or account.

sections.title: Two approaches at Tempus
paragraphs: Tempus describes the round ICE Smart 3.0 1.20 Gold-Beige, reference 025115, with an AMOLED screen and built-in GPS. Consider it if you want a smartwatch screen and notifications. Check that its GPS functions, route export and battery life with GPS meet your expectations; we publish no measured endurance.

The G-Shock GBD-200-2ER takes a different approach with a digital display and phone-linked activity functions. Casio explains that smartphone GPS can calibrate distance calculated from the accelerometer. Do not buy it expecting the same built-in GPS hardware listed for the ICE Smart.

sections.title: Battery and app belong in the decision
paragraphs: Charging routine can matter as much as the dial design. Ask which battery-life figure matches your use: brightness, notifications and GPS can change the stated conditions. Keep the correct charger and follow the instructions.
Also look at app permissions, export options and how to delete your account if you stop using the service. These details matter when a watch depends on software, even when you love its appearance.

sections.title: For sport, check the exact requirement
paragraphs: A regular running routine may require route recording, pace information or specific exports. Do not assume a watch covers all of these because its listing mentions sport or GPS. Confirm the function in its instructions or with Tempus before ordering.

The ICE Smart’s listed IP68 rating does not automatically authorise swimming or diving. Activity indicators are not a substitute for a medical device either. Choose for your actual routine and the limits of the exact model.

etancheite-montre-3-5-10-20-atm.title: 3, 5, 10 or 20 ATM: which watch for water?
etancheite-montre-3-5-10-20-atm.description: Rain, pools and holidays: understand the markings, the strap and the precautions that matter before choosing.

sections.title: Start with your day, not a number
paragraphs: Do you want a watch for the office, weekly swimming or a seaside holiday? These are different requirements. Choose the activity that matters before comparing dials. A dress watch on leather can be an excellent everyday choice without following you into a pool.

The metres in a listing are not a depth to reach with any watch. Read the marking alongside the exact manual, strap and watch condition. A 20 ATM marking does not automatically make it a diving watch.

sections.title: The useful distinctions
paragraphs: 3 bar / 3 ATM: everyday splashes, not swimming. Citizen’s usage chart places this level in occasional contact with water. Choose another watch for a swim.
5 bar / 5 ATM: read the manual before the pool. Citizen permits ordinary swimming at this level for the relevant watches, but not skin diving. A leather strap can still be damaged by immersion.

10 or 20 bar / ATM: more possibilities, not every sport. Casio’s general chart permits swimming at these levels but excludes scuba diving for ordinary water-resistant watches. The exact manual governs activities and button operation.

sections.title: Three watches that show the difference
paragraphs: Tempus lists the Bambino RA-AC0M04Y with 3 ATM and leather: choose it for its dressy appearance. The Tsuyosa NJ0150-81E is listed at 5 ATM. The GA-2100-1A1ER has a 20 bar marking and resin strap. These illustrate different constructions, not a universal quality ranking.

Before buying for a water activity, find the exact manual and check the supplied strap too. For scuba diving, seek a reference explicitly designed for that use: Citizen distinguishes ISO 6425 diving watches from ordinary watches listed at 20 bar.

sections.title: Showers, seawater and care
paragraphs: Casio advises against bathing, heat and contact with soaps; leave the watch off for showers and saunas. Do not operate wet or submerged controls unless the specific manual permits it.

After seawater exposure, follow the manufacturer’s rinsing instructions. Seiko advises fresh water and a cloth, avoiding a direct tap jet. Seals and impacts affect resistance over time: after work on the watch or if in doubt, have it checked before swimming again.

sections.title: Filter without guessing
paragraphs: Our catalogue can select a minimum explicit 5, 10 or 20 bar / ATM marking from Tempus data. Listings with no usable value are excluded; metre-only values are not converted. This creates a shortlist to investigate, not certification for water use.
